Dear Secretary Reese:

        Pursuant to sections 205 and 219 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)1 and Part 35 of the
regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “the Commission”),2
Anchor Point West, LLC (“Anchor West”) respectfully requests that the Commission:

       1.      Approve Anchor West’s initial Transmission Owner Tariff (“TO Tariff”), formula
               rate template (“Template”), and formula rate implementation protocols
               (“Protocols”, and together with the Template, the “Formula Rate”), to calculate
               Anchor West’s annual transmission revenue requirement (“TRR”) to be
               incorporated into the Transmission Access Charge (“TAC”) under the California
               Independent System Operator Corporation (“CAISO”) Tariff (the “CAISO
               Tariff”);

       2.      Authorize Anchor West to use three incentive rate treatments: a Regulatory Asset
               Incentive, a Hypothetical Capital Structure Incentive, and a Regional Transmission
               Organization (“RTO”) Participation Incentive (defined separately below, and
               together, the “Incentives”); and

       3.      Authorize later-formed subsidiaries in CAISO of Anchor West’s parent company,
               Anchor Point Transmission, LLC (“Anchor Point Transmission”) to adopt the
               Formula Rate in connection with transmission projects in CAISO (such affiliates,
               the “Anchor Point Transmission CAISO Subsidiaries”).

         Anchor West’s requests are just and reasonable. FERC has regularly granted such requests
for similarly situated new-entrant transmission development companies. The Formula Rate will
calculate Anchor West’s TRR, consistent with the CAISO Tariff. Consistent with Commission
policy, the Incentives will provide a level playing field for Anchor West to establish financial
principles that incumbent transmission owners currently have in place. FERC’s authorization for
Anchor Point Transmission to adopt the formula rate for Anchor Point Transmission CAISO
Subsidiaries will conserve Commission resources to the public benefit.

         Anchor West respectfully submits that the Commission should approve the Formula Rate,
the Incentives, and authorization for the Anchor Point Transmission CAISO Subsidiaries to use
the same Formula Rate and Incentives without relitigation (the “Filing”) as just and reasonable to
facilitate urgently needed transmission expansion under CAISO’s competitive framework.

I.    BACKGROUND

        A. Anchor Point Transmission and Anchor West TO Tariff

         Anchor Point Transmission is a new-entrant transmission development platform owned by
ArcLight Infrastructure Partners Fund VIII-A, L.P. (and its parallel funds) (together, “ArcLight
Fund VIII”) and managed by ArcLight Capital Partners, LLC (“ArcLight”). ArcLight is a leading
manager of infrastructure investment funds specialized in developing, managing, and operating
critical power infrastructure.3 ArcLight formed Anchor Point Transmission to (i) participate in
Commission-approved competitive solicitations to develop electric transmission, and (ii) partner
with electric utilities to solve transmission issues, optimize electric utility systems, and help
manage costs on these systems to the benefit of ratepayers.4 Anchor Point Transmission is focused
on the needs of small to mid-sized investor-owned utilities, municipal utilities, cooperatives, and
public power agencies.

       Anchor West is a non-incumbent transmission development company, focused on
transmission needs in the CAISO region. Anchor West plans to independently, and with partners,
pursue development opportunities in the CAISO Transmission Planning Process (“TPP”).5 With
the support of ArcLight Fund VIII, Anchor West is expertly positioned to devote financial and
operational resources to enhance the reliability of the transmission system. Though ArcLight
managed funds have invested in transmission projects in the past, ArcLight is not currently

        B. CAISO’s Competitive Solicitation Process

        CAISO undertakes a comprehensive regional transmission planning process through the
TPP. The TPP is a fair and open regional planning process that considers and evaluates projects
for reliability, congestion relief, and public policy transmission needs. CAISO’s TPP includes
significant stakeholder participation, and the Commission deemed it compliant with Order Nos.
890 and 1000.8 Approval of this Filing would facilitate Anchor West’s participation in the TPP.
The TO Tariff and Formula Rate are designed to accommodate the recovery of costs associated
with any transmission projects Anchor West may be assigned through the TPP.

        Through the competitive solicitation process, CAISO selects approved project sponsors to
finance, construct, own, operate and maintain transmission solutions included in the transmission
plan approved by the CAISO’s Board of Governors (the “CAISO Board”). Following the CAISO
Board’s approval of the plan, project sponsors will submit proposals which must include plan of
service details and supporting information.

II.   SUMMARY OF REQUESTED ACTIONS

        A. TO Tariff

        Anchor West requests that the Commission accept for filing its proposed TO Tariff,
effective December 1, 2026. In accordance with the CAISO Tariff and CAISO’s governing
documents, Anchor West will execute the Transmission Control Agreement (“TCA”) and become
a CAISO Participating Transmission Owner (“PTO”) once it acquires rights to transmission assets
or is awarded a project in CAISO. The TO Tariff establishes the framework for Anchor West’s
participation as a non-load-serving PTO in the CAISO. The proposed TO Tariff is based on other
transmission owner tariffs accepted for filing by the Commission and is consistent with FERC
precedent.9 The details of the TO Tariff and the underlying legal precedent that supports it are
discussed in Section IV below.

         B. Formula Rate

        Anchor West requests that the Commission accept for filing its proposed non-
levelized Formula Rate, effective December 1, 2026. The Formula Rate will calculate Anchor
West’s TRR for inclusion in the TAC. The proposed Formula Rate is based on other formula
rates accepted for filing by the Commission and is consistent with FERC precedent.10 The
details of the Formula Rate and its grounding in precedent are discussed in Section IV below.

        C. Incentive Rate Treatments

      Anchor West requests that the Commission authorize the following Incentives pursuant to
FPA section 205 and 219:

        (1) Recovery of all prudently incurred pre-commercial, start-up and formation costs, and
            establishment of a regulatory asset including all expenses that are incurred prior to the
            time costs are first flowed through to customers under the CAISO Tariff (“Regulatory
            Asset Incentive”);

        (2) Use of a hypothetical capital structure of 60% equity and 40% debt until Anchor West
            first holds rights to transmission assets that are placed in service (“Hypothetical Capital
            Structure Incentive”), subject to a voluntary cap on equity of 60%; and

        (3) A 50 basis-point return on equity (“ROE”) adder to the base ROE (“RTO Participation
            Incentive”, and together with the Regulatory Asset Incentive and Hypothetical Capital
            Structure Incentive, the “Incentives”), conditioned on Anchor West turning over
            functional control of all transmission assets it develops or in which it holds rights to
            CAISO.

        Anchor West asks that the Commission approve the requested Incentives by December 1,
2026 so that Anchor West may (1) obtain regulatory certainty for application of incentives
to transmission projects that are approved under the CAISO Tariff, in furtherance of Anchor
West’s participation in CAISO’s TPP; and (2) credibly plan for partnerships with electric utility
partners, with the level of regulatory certainty required to access capital markets.

           D. Authorization for Anchor Point Transmission CAISO Subsidiaries to Use the
             Same Formula Rate and Requested Incentives

        In the future, Anchor Point Transmission may create subsidiaries for certain transmission
projects in CAISO. Thus, Anchor West requests authorization for any Anchor Point Transmission
CAISO Subsidiaries to use the same Formula Rate and the same requested Incentives that are
approved for Anchor West in this proceeding. Each such subsidiary would file for PTO status and
execute the TCA separately. Grounded in precedent, this prior approval would allow replication
of the accepted formula rate and use of the same Incentives for Anchor Point Transmission CAISO
Subsidiaries operating in the same region without relitigating these issues.11

III. CONTENTS OF FILING

       In addition to this letter, which provides a detailed description of the approvals requested
and the bases for those requests, this filing contains the following components:

          Attachment A:           TO Tariff with Formula Rate Template and Formula Rate
                                  Implementation Protocols

          Attachment B:           Formula Rate Template in Excel File Format

          Attachment C:           Direct Testimony and Exhibits of Justin Campbell (description of

                                  treatments) (Exhibit Nos. APW-100 – APW-101);

          Attachment D:           Direct Testimony and Exhibits of Kurt Strunk (return on equity;
                                  transmission incentives) (Exhibit Nos. APW-200 – APW-216);

          Attachment E:           Direct Testimony and Exhibits of Walter Hopkins (Formula Rate
                                  and Protocols) (Exhibit Nos. APW-300 – APW-301);

          Attachment F:           Direct Testimony and Exhibits of Ned Allis (depreciation rates)
                                  (Exhibit Nos. APW-400 – APW-402); and

          Attachment G:           Attestation Required by 18 C.F.R. § 35.13(d)(6).

IV.     THE PROPOSED TO TARIFF IS JUST AND REASONABLE

          Anchor West requests that the Commission accept its TO Tariff, including its proposed
     forward-looking Formula Rate, for filing effective December 1, 2026. Anchor West proposes to

rates.12 Formula rates are the baseline standard for transmission-only utilities, providing cost
transparency via the flow-through of inputs from the transmission owner’s filed, regulated balance
sheet: the FERC Form 1. For purposes of the TO Tariff and the CAISO Tariff, Anchor West is a
non-load-serving PTO and has no end-use Customers.

       As shown below, Anchor West’s proposed Formula Rate, including the Template and
Protocols, is just and reasonable, consistent with FERC precedent.

        A. Formula Rate Design

       Anchor West’s proposed forward-looking Formula Rate13 is similar to formula rates the
Commission has accepted for other competitive transmission developers in CAISO.14 The
Template is the mechanism for calculating Anchor West’s projected and actual net revenue
requirements in accordance with the procedures described in Anchor West’s Protocols.15 The
Protocols are discussed in Section IV.E below.

        The Template determines the TRR based on operation and maintenance expenses,
administrative and general expense, depreciation expense, taxes other than income taxes, income
tax allowance, return on rate base, and any incentive rate adjustments, less any revenue credits and
agreed-to competitive adjustments for particular projects.

        Anchor West is a pass-through entity for income tax purposes. Before revenues are first
collected under the Formula Rate and income taxes are first required to be recorded, a subset of
Anchor West’s upstream parents will be classified, pursuant to an election under the Internal
Revenue Service’s entity-classification regulations, as entities taxable as corporations and subject
to corporate income tax. A portion of the income or losses from Anchor West will be includable
on such parents’ income tax return, and such parents will be obligated to pay corporate income tax
on such amounts. Thus, Anchor West will record income tax expenses and accumulated deferred
income taxes in its separate books of account even though a subset of its parents will pay these
taxes as costs-incurred.16 Accordingly, the Template provides for an income tax allowance that is

         B. ROE

       Based on application of the Commission’s approved ROE methodology,19 Anchor West
requests a base ROE of 12.49%, which is supported by the analysis and testimony of Mr. Kurt
Strunk.20 The Formula Rate includes a fixed ROE value of 12.99%, consisting of a base ROE of
12.49%, reflecting capital market conditions, and a 50 basis-point adder for participating in a
Commission-approved RTO.

         An ROE sufficient to attract the necessary capital is critical to Anchor West, as it is a start-
up transmission company with no business history, no established credit rating or other evidence
of creditworthiness, no debt repayment history, and no earnings history. Anchor West’s ability to
attract financing, including equity and debt from banks, bond investors, and/or other lenders, will
be based primarily on these financial stakeholders’ expectations for a transmission project to
deliver stable projected cash flows.21 Anchor West’s access to capital is dependent on the strength
and predictability of the regulatory framework and ratemaking mechanisms applicable to Anchor
West that will allow it to predict and model project returns and assess risks in connection with its
investments.

        In addition to the risks applicable to any new entrant transmission developer, certain risk
factors are relevant to transmission development in the CAISO region, including the potential costs
associated with wildfire resiliency measures and California’s inverse condemnation doctrine,
which permits property owners, under certain circumstances, to recover wildfire-related property
damage caused by public improvements even absent a finding of negligence or foreseeability.22
As Mr. Strunk explains, these considerations are among the factors that capital markets may weigh
when assessing investment in electric transmission infrastructure in the State.23 Furthermore,
Senate Bill 254 established a framework for the ongoing evaluation and restructuring of wildfire
prevention oversight and mitigation standards, creating significant long-term uncertainty for
entities developing transmission infrastructure in California.24 Because the applicable standards

         Mr. Strunk’s results from the DCF and CAPM produce a composite zone of reasonableness
ranging from 9.42% to 14.44%.26 Mr. Strunk concludes that a base ROE of 12.49% is just and
reasonable for Anchor West to attract financing. Anchor West’s rate of return must be sufficient

      For all of the reasons above, the Commission should accept the proposed base ROE of
12.49% for the Anchor West Formula Rate.

         C. Depreciation Rates

        As noted above, Anchor West is a new entrant in the competitive transmission development
market, and it does not yet hold rights to transmission facilities. Thus, Anchor West does not have
its own historical data on facility service life or net salvage estimates on which to support a
depreciation study. In similar circumstances where an applicant did not yet hold rights to
transmission facilities, the applicant has used, and the Commission has accepted, proxy
depreciation rates based on estimated service lives and net salvage rates developed for each
depreciable group.27 As explained by Mr. Ned Allis, Anchor West proposes to use representative
depreciation rates (Exhibit No. APW-402) for the electric transmission accounts developed from
the expected function and characteristics of the electric transmission facilities, information
provided by Anchor West, and depreciation parameters used for similar transmission assets by
other electric utilities. These proxy depreciation rates would remain in effect until changed through
a limited-scope FPA section 205 filing based on a future depreciation study of assets in which
Anchor West or its affiliates hold rights within CAISO, as the Protocols provide, to analyze their
life characteristics.28

         D. Competitive Project Adjustments

         The Template proposed by Anchor West incorporates flexibility to make project-specific
competitive adjustments to the TRR.29 Anchor West may develop transmission projects for which
it has offered competitive adjustments for projects that, if accepted by CAISO, would change what
could otherwise be collected under the Formula Rate as it relates to the awarded project. For
example, such adjustments could include concessions on project ROE or capital structure, or a cap
on project costs or revenue requirements. Anchor West may also seek discrete incentive rate
treatments by separately filing for specific transmission projects that CAISO awards to it. Any
such adjustments will be reflected, through lines 48 and 48a (page 3 of 5) of the Template, in the

         E. Formula Rate Implementation Protocols

        Mr. Hopkins describes the Protocols for populating the Template and updating the TRR
calculation in his testimony.33 The Protocols are transparent, consistent with the Commission’s
guidance on protocols for forward-looking formula rates,34 and will provide Anchor West’s
customers meaningful transparency, with procedural safeguards to facilitate the annual review for
assessment of the inputs to the TRR.

       The proposed Formula Rate is forward-looking, determined based on projected accounting
values and then trued up after the relevant rate year based on actual accounting values. A forward-

        The Protocols provide that, to calculate Anchor West’s TRR, Anchor West forecasts the
values that populate the Template for each calendar year (“Rate Year”) and determines a true-up
of the forecasted values after the actual data becomes available on the FERC Form No. 1. Any
difference between the projected TRR and the actual TRR for the relevant Rate Year will be
reflected in a true-up adjustment to the following year’s TRR. Thus, for example, Anchor West
would determine in 2028 (after submitting its FERC Form No. 1 covering 2027 in April 2028)
how the actual TRR for 2027 differed from the projected TRR for 2027. Any difference, along
with interest calculated in accordance with section 35.19a of the Commission’s regulations, will
be reflected as a true-up adjustment to the projected 2029 TRR. The differences between the TRR
and the receipts from CAISO are reconciled separately through the Transmission Revenue
Balancing Account Adjustment under the TO Tariff. This ensures that neither the customers nor
Anchor West are harmed if the projected TRR differs from the actual TRR.35

        Anchor West’s Protocols are consistent with the Commission’s instructions to other
entities with respect to (i) opportunities to participate in Anchor West’s information exchange
process; (ii) the transparency of the information exchange; and (iii) the ability of interested parties
to challenge Anchor West’s implementation of the Formula Rate.36 The Protocols establish a
transparent process governing the annual informational filing, information exchange between
Anchor West and interested parties, and procedures for informal and formal challenges to Anchor
West’s implementation of the Formula Rate.

         As discussed above, Anchor West does not currently hold rights to any transmission
facilities upon which to prepare a depreciation study, and thus relies, in the first instance, on
representative depreciation rates developed from parameters used for similar transmission assets,
as described in the testimony of Mr. Allis.37 Further, Anchor West does not currently have PBOP

V.    ACCOUNTING

        Mr. Justin Campbell (Exhibit No. APW-100) provides an overview of Anchor West’s
general accounting in support of the Anchor West Formula Rate. Anchor West will utilize the
accrual method of accounting as required by Generally Accepted Accounting Principles to record
revenues and costs, which will be recorded in accounts prescribed by the Commission’s Uniform
System of Accounts.40 As Mr. Campbell explains, Anchor Point Transmission has established
formal processes to review and approve all costs, including costs related to Anchor West. Those
costs are reviewed periodically to track expenses and monitor charges to Anchor West.41

the Hypothetical Capital Structure Incentive by new entrant competitive transmission developers,

facilitate the formation of additional entities for purposes of participating as nonincumbent

        Use of a hypothetical capital structure until such time as Anchor West first holds rights to
transmission assets that are placed in service is appropriate to offset risks and to improve Anchor
West’s access to capital. At first, Anchor West intends to operate with 100 percent capital infusions
from its parent company. As construction on the first project progresses, Anchor West is expected
to require additional capital contributions. As Mr. Campbell explains,56 debt-to-equity ratio can be
volatile as new debt and equity are invested. Because of the initial reliance on capital contributions,
which will persist even after Anchor West first holds rights to transmission assets that are placed
in service, Anchor West will cap the equity portion of the cost of capital calculation to the lower
of 60% or the equity portion of Anchor West’s actual capital structure. Anchor West’s equity cap
proposal is consistent with past Commission orders involving requests from similarly situated
startup entities; in fact, two decades of precedent have allowed operating transmission companies
to maintain actual capital structures at this level.57

equity ratio for ratemaking purposes during construction provides certainty and improves access
to capital.58 In PATH, the Commission found that the use of a hypothetical capital structure during
construction “will result in lower debt costs for the company, while also permitting it to vary its
financing vehicles to the needs of the construction process, including such issues as timing of
expenditures, regulatory developments, and changes in financial market conditions.”59 It also
found the hypothetical capital structure approach during the construction period is a “pragmatic
approach to address . . . fluctuating capital structure” at the outset of a project’s development.60

1, 2026. The Filing is consistent with Commission policy, as more fully supported by the
testimony and associated exhibits included as part of this filing. Further, Anchor West is
concurrently submitting an eTariff record for the purpose of ensuring a 60-day action date from
the Commission, pursuant to section 205 of the FPA.72

Commission order on this request.

transmission bids in the CAISO process. Acceptance of the Formula Rate and authorization of the
requested incentive rate treatments will help put Anchor West on an equal footing with incumbent
transmission developers that already have formula transmission rates in place.
